def predict(parameters, state, history):
    # Anchored Anti-Validity Frugality with Validity-Respecting Leak
    # (frozen-discipline variant).
    #
    # Minimal-diff edit of the accepted iter-1 base:
    #   (a) The validity-respecting leak is now TRIAL-CONDITIONAL: it is
    #       eligible only when the anti-validity cascade's first
    #       discriminating expert j* on this trial carries a strictly
    #       INTERIOR validity (min + 0.10 < val[j*] < max - 0.10), and
    #       it is implemented as a PROBABILITY MIXTURE (no Bernoulli
    #       draw) with ceiling 0.18.
    #   (b) A DISTINCT-DESIGN BONUS b_distinct multiplies beta_eff when
    #       all validities are distinct (tie designs untouched).
    #   (c) Response-discipline / diffusion parameters are FROZEN at
    #       narrow windows that reproduce the accepted base's behavior;
    #       only rho_leak and b_distinct are genuinely free.
    stim = np.asarray(state, dtype=float)
    if stim.ndim != 2 or stim.shape[0] != 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Expects a (2, n_features) stimulus; got shape {stim.shape}."
        )
    n_features = stim.shape[1]

    val = np.asarray(parameters["validities"], dtype=float).ravel()
    if val.shape[0] != n_features:
        raise ValueError(
            f"validities length {val.shape[0]} != n_features {n_features}."
        )

    beta = float(parameters["beta"])
    boost = float(parameters["boost"])
    b_distinct = float(parameters["b_distinct"])
    epsilon = float(parameters["epsilon"])
    gamma = float(parameters["gamma"])
    kappa = float(parameters["kappa"])
    sigma_h = float(parameters["sigma_h"])
    rho_leak = float(parameters["rho_leak"])
    tie_break = float(parameters["tie_break"])

    zeta = np.asarray(parameters["zeta"], dtype=float).ravel()
    if zeta.shape[0] != n_features:
        raise ValueError(
            f"zeta length {zeta.shape[0]} != n_features {n_features}."
        )

    # ---- helper: average-tie ranks ----
    def avg_ranks(x):
        n = x.shape[0]
        srt = np.argsort(x, kind="stable")
        ranks = np.empty(n, dtype=float)
        i = 0
        while i < n:
            j = i
            while j + 1 < n and x[srt[j + 1]] == x[srt[i]]:
                j += 1
            ranks[srt[i:j + 1]] = 0.5 * (i + j)  # 0-indexed average rank
            i = j + 1
        return ranks

    # ---- positional-salience gradient (early-listed experts favored) ----
    if n_features > 1:
        sal = ((n_features - 1 - np.arange(n_features, dtype=float))
               / (n_features - 1.0)) - 0.5
    else:
        sal = np.zeros(1, dtype=float)

    # ---- binding ambiguity: A = 1 - |Spearman(position, validity)| ----
    if n_features > 1:
        ranks = avg_ranks(val)
        pos_r = np.arange(n_features, dtype=float)
        vp = pos_r - pos_r.mean()
        vr = ranks - ranks.mean()
        denom = np.sqrt(float((vp * vp).sum()) * float((vr * vr).sum()))
        if denom > 1e-12:
            rho = float((vp * vr).sum()) / denom
        else:
            rho = 0.0
        ambiguity = 1.0 - abs(rho)
    else:
        ambiguity = 0.0

    # ---- reversal coherence: |Spearman(validity, validity[::-1])| ----
    if n_features > 1:
        ranks_v = avg_ranks(val)
        ranks_r = avg_ranks(val[::-1])
        dv = ranks_v - ranks_v.mean()
        dr = ranks_r - ranks_r.mean()
        denom2 = np.sqrt(float((dv * dv).sum()) * float((dr * dr).sum()))
        if denom2 > 1e-12:
            rho_rev = float((dv * dr).sum()) / denom2
        else:
            rho_rev = 0.0
        coherence = abs(rho_rev)
    else:
        coherence = 0.0

    # ---- mean adjacent validity gap over UNIQUE validities ----
    uvals = np.unique(val)
    if uvals.size > 1:
        mean_gap = float(np.mean(np.diff(np.sort(uvals))))
    else:
        mean_gap = 0.0

    distinct = (uvals.size == n_features)

    # ---- gap-proportional anchoring ratios (verbatim from base) ----
    ref_gap = 0.10
    gap_ratio = np.ones(n_features, dtype=float)
    if distinct and n_features > 1:
        srt = np.argsort(val, kind="stable")
        sv = val[srt]
        gs = np.ones(n_features, dtype=float)
        for r in range(n_features):
            g = 0.0
            if r > 0:
                g += sv[r] - sv[r - 1]          # gap to next weaker
            if r < n_features - 1:
                g += sv[r + 1] - sv[r]          # gap to next stronger
            gs[srt[r]] = max(g, 0.05)           # numerical floor
        gap_ratio = np.minimum(ref_gap / gs, 2.0)

    amb3 = ambiguity * ambiguity * ambiguity

    pos = np.arange(n_features)
    secondary = pos if tie_break < 0.8 else (n_features - 1 - pos)

    a, b = stim[0], stim[1]

    def cascade_winner(order):
        for j in order:
            if a[j] > b[j]:
                return 0
            if b[j] > a[j]:
                return 1
        return None

    # ---- STABLE anti-validity weights (no momentary noise): used ONLY
    # to locate this trial's anti-validity carrier j* for the leak gate.
    w_stable = -val + gamma * sal
    if distinct and ambiguity > 0.0:
        w_stable = w_stable + amb3 * kappa * gap_ratio * sigma_h * zeta
    order_stable = np.lexsort((secondary, -w_stable))

    j_star = None
    for j in order_stable:
        if a[j] != b[j]:
            j_star = int(j)
            break

    # ---- TRIAL-CONDITIONAL leak eligibility: strictly interior carrier.
    # Weakest-expert carriers (val <= min + 0.10) and near-top carriers
    # (val >= max - 0.10) switch the leak OFF; only genuinely mid-
    # validity carriers let the TTB leak fire. Ceiling 0.18.
    leak_q = 0.0
    if j_star is not None and n_features > 1:
        vmin = float(val.min())
        vmax = float(val.max())
        if (vmin + 0.10) < val[j_star] < (vmax - 0.10):
            leak_q = float(min(rho_leak * coherence * mean_gap, 0.18))

    # ---- per-trial subjective hierarchy (momentary diffusion added) ----
    w = w_stable.copy()
    if distinct and ambiguity > 0.0:
        xi = np.random.normal(0.0, 1.0, size=n_features)
        w = w + amb3 * kappa * gap_ratio * xi
    order_anti = np.lexsort((secondary, -w))
    winner_anti = cascade_winner(order_anti)

    n_opts = 2
    if winner_anti is None:
        # No discriminating cue: pure guess (lapse mixing leaves a
        # uniform unchanged).
        return np.ones(n_opts) / float(n_opts)

    # ---- design-scaled response discipline with DISTINCT-DESIGN BONUS ----
    beta_eff = beta * (1.0 + boost * (1.0 - ambiguity))
    if distinct:
        beta_eff = beta_eff * (1.0 + b_distinct)

    def score_prob(winner):
        scores = np.array([1.0, 0.0]) if winner == 0 else np.array([0.0, 1.0])
        z = beta_eff * (scores - scores.max())
        e = np.exp(z)
        return e / e.sum()

    p_core = score_prob(winner_anti)

    # ---- VALIDITY-RESPECTING LEAK as a probability mixture (no
    # Bernoulli draw -> lower Monte Carlo variance in simulated metrics).
    if leak_q > 0.0:
        order_ttb = np.lexsort((secondary, -val))
        winner_ttb = cascade_winner(order_ttb)
        if winner_ttb is not None and winner_ttb != winner_anti:
            p_core = (1.0 - leak_q) * p_core + leak_q * score_prob(winner_ttb)

    return (1.0 - epsilon) * p_core + epsilon * (np.ones(n_opts) / float(n_opts))
next_theory.rationale: This is a surgical edit of the accepted iter-1 base implementing the iter-3 critic's prescription, whose two prior rejection diagnoses I take as ground truth: (i) the leak-gate DIRECTION was empirically right both times (Exps 3/9/10 moved correctly in isolation), but (ii) range-narrowing failed twice as a drift-control strategy because the leak changed the joint likelihood landscape and dragged the shared response-discipline parameters (beta/boost) upward, inflating p_f and regressing every decider-follow metric (Exps 4, 5, 6, 10, 7, 13). I therefore change the drift-control STRATEGY, not just the ranges. (1) FREEZE: beta, boost, epsilon, gamma, kappa, sigma_h are confined to narrow windows centered on the base's mid-range values (I verified analytically that mid-range values reproduce the base's Exp-5 follow of ~0.68 and Exp-3 anti-follow of ~0.71, i.e., the base's operating point), so only rho_leak and the new b_distinct are effectively free. (2) SYMMETRIC INTERIOR GATE (delta = 0.10 hardcoded): the leak is eligible only when the anti-validity cascade's carrier j* on this trial satisfies min + 0.10 < val[j*] < max - 0.10. Hand-traced consequences: on Exp 3 the carrier is always the 0.5-validity minimum expert -> leak provably OFF -> Exp 3 must stay at (or slightly above, via the distinct bonus) the base's value, serving as the freeze regression test; on Exp 6 the carriers are the 0.6-validity minima -> leak OFF; on Exp 7 the design's validity set {0.6, 0.65, 0.85, 0.9, 0.95} contains NO strictly interior values, so the leak never fires there — this removes iter-2's wrong-direction T11 flip while restoring the base's pure anti-follow; on Exp 9 the dissociating carriers are weak experts (<= 0.7 = min + 0.10) -> leak OFF, protecting the near-exact 0.427 fit; on Exp 8 the interior carriers (0.75, 0.8) let the leak flip toward TTB exactly where TTB opposes the reversed cascade, pushing the metric more negative as the data demand. (3) PROBABILITY MIXTURE instead of a per-trial Bernoulli for the leak (numerically equivalent, lower Monte Carlo variance), with ceiling lowered to 0.18 and rho_leak widened to [0.5, 3.0] so the cap — not an attenuated coherence x gap product — does the bounding on high-product designs (Exp 13's product is ~0.097, so the leak can reach the cap there if the fit wants it). (4) DISTINCT-DESIGN BONUS b_distinct in [0, 0.25] multiplying beta_eff when all validities are distinct: this is the orthogonal p_f knob the critic prescribed, along the axis (distinct vs tied) the data actually support — it raises follow on the distinct designs that undershoot (Exps 1, 3, 10, 15) while leaving the tie designs (Exps 5, 6, 7, 13) exactly at base behavior, preventing the cross-contamination that killed iters 2 and 3. (5) Exp 10 is the top-priority target (largest base miss, -31): the interior gate switches the leak off on its weakest-carrier agreeing cells, and the bounded distinct bonus raises the mean follow toward the real level without the uncontrolled inflation that overshot iter-3 to 150.9. I accept Exp 13 (~0.30 vs 0.15) and the Exp 7 structural cap (~-0.20 vs -0.31) as residual misses shared by every one-reason competitor, per the critic's explicit instruction not to trade the winnable experiments for them. All changes stay strictly inside the prescribed Anchored Anti-Validity Frugality with Validity-Respecting Leak family.

experiment.rationale:
GOAL: Quantitatively dissociate Anti-Validity Frugality with Diffuse Positional-Salience Heterogeneity, momentary-diffusion variant (advocated) from Anchored Anti-Validity Frugality with Validity-Respecting Leak, frozen-discipline variant (competing). The two theories share the anti-validity one-reason core, the same A^3 ambiguity gate, comparable diffusion magnitudes, and the same tie-anchoring rule — so diffusion-structure axes cannot cleanly separate them (at any ambiguity where the advocated diffuses, the competing's gap-scaled noise is of the same order). The ONE structural mechanism with diverging, design-forced commitments is the competing's TRIAL-CONDITIONAL VALIDITY-RESPECTING LEAK: a probability mixture (ceiling 0.18) toward the standard TTB (descending-validity) decider that fires ONLY when the anti-validity cascade's first discriminating expert carries a strictly INTERIOR validity (min+0.10 < val < max-0.10). The advocated has NO such mechanism: in the anchored regime its follow probability is p_f toward the anti-decider on EVERY discriminating trial, flat over decider validity, decider position, margin, and coalition size. The design therefore engineers the anchored regime and maximizes the competing's committed leak strength, then tests a flat-vs-dipped follow profile.

SETUP: 6 features with validities [0.50, 0.50, 0.75, 0.75, 1.00, 1.00] (f0..f5), monotone ascending with exact ties. Consequences (both models' own formulas, average-tie ranks): Spearman(position, validity) = 0.956, so binding ambiguity A = 0.044 and A^3 = 8.4e-5 — both theories' distortion channels are switched off entirely (their own rules: distortion requires all-distinct validities AND ambiguity > 0; ties anchor the distrust order in both). Every within-tied-pair gap (0.25) dwarfs both theories' gamma*sal tilts (advocated <= 0.072, competing <= 0.018), so the consultation order is EXACTLY the anti-validity cascade {f0,f1}(50%) -> {f2,f3}(75%) -> {f4,f5}(100%) in both models, with tie_break inert (tied cues never oppose in any trial). Reversal coherence = 0.956; mean_gap over unique validities = 0.25 — the MAXIMUM achievable while keeping an interior validity (three unique values spanning [0.5, 1.0]). Hence the competing's leak probability q = min(rho_leak * 0.956 * 0.25, 0.18) is forced into [0.120, 0.18] for ANY rho_leak in [0.5, 3.0]: the competing CANNOT switch its leak off in this design. Its p_f = (1-eps)*sigmoid(beta*(1+boost*0.956)) + eps/2 lies in [0.708, 0.754] (distinct-design bonus inert because validities are tied). The advocated's p_f lies in [0.59, 0.84] (beta in [0.5,1.9], eps in [0.08,0.24]).

CELL FAMILIES. (L) LEAK CELLS (T1-T8, four exact A/B mirror pairs): the anti-decider is an interior 0.75 cue and a 100% expert discriminates in OPPOSITION (all 50% cues tied, so the carrier is unambiguous). T1/T2: f2 vs f4; T3/T4: f3 vs f5 (position-balanced replicate); T5/T6: both 0.75s vs both 100%s (tally margin 0); T7/T8: one 0.75 vs both 100%s (margin -1). Advocated: p(carrier's option) = p_f on ALL eight. Competing: p(carrier's option) = (1-q)*p_f + q*(1-p_f) in [0.633, 0.693] — a DIP of q*(2p_f-1) in [0.050, 0.093] relative to its own no-leak follow rate. (C) CONTROL CELLS (T9-T16): T9/T10 — interior 0.75 carrier with the 100% expert CONCURRING (leak eligible but winner_ttb = winner_anti, so no mixture): both theories p_f; this matches decider validity with the leak cells, isolating TTB opposition as the dip's cause. T11/T12 — WEAKEST carrier (50%) opposed by the 100% expert: leak OFF (carrier not interior); both theories p_f toward the 50% expert. T13/T14 — weakest carrier (50%) opposed by the interior 0.75 expert: leak OFF; a generic always-on TTB mixture would dip here too, but the competing's trial-conditional gate does not — this cell separates the leak from any unconditional validity-respecting contamination. T15 — lone interior decider (only f2 discriminates; TTB concurs): p_f. T16 — full tie: exactly 0.50 in both, anchoring lapse and side bias.

SIGNATURE 1 — THE LEAK DIP (central, two-sided, parameter-forced): define each subject's carrier-follow rate (choices matching the anti-validity decider's option). Advocated: EXACTLY EQUAL follow rates on leak and control cells (both are p_f; no mechanism in the advocated depends on the decider's validity rank, its position, or the opposition's validity). Competing: follow rate on the eight leak cells is lower by q*(2p_f-1) in [0.050, 0.093] — bounded AWAY FROM ZERO by its own gate formulas (q >= 0.120 is forced by rho_leak >= 0.5, coherence 0.956, mean_gap 0.25). The prediction intervals on this within-subject paired contrast are DISJOINT: [0, 0] vs [0.050, 0.093]. With 48 leak trials and 42 control trials per subject, a population dip estimate of ~0 (CI within +/-0.03) falsifies the competing at any parameter setting; a dip >= 0.05 falsifies the advocated, which cannot produce it.

SIGNATURE 2 — THE CONDITIONALITY TRIAD (specificity of the dip): the competing predicts the dip ONLY on the conjunction (interior carrier AND top-validity opposition): T1 vs T9/T15 (interior carrier, opposition removed -> no dip), T1 vs T11 (opposition retained, carrier demoted to weakest -> no dip), T1 vs T13 (higher-validity opposition retained, carrier weakest -> no dip). The advocated predicts no dip in any cell. An unconditional partial-TTB mixture (the natural simpler competitor) dips on T11 AND T13 as well — so the triad also protects the dissociation from being absorbed by a less conditional theory.

SIGNATURE 3 — FLAT PROFILE OVER MARGIN AND COALITION (shared one-reason core + integration kill): across T1 (margin 0, 1v1), T5 (margin 0, 2v2), T7 (margin -1) both theories predict IDENTICAL carrier-follow rates — no margin effect, no coalition-size effect. Tallying is pinned to EXACTLY 0.50 on T5/T6 (margin 0) and below 0.5 on T7, while both one-reason theories predict ~p_f toward the 0.75-cue option — any consistent preference on T5/T6 falsifies the entire integration family, and any reliable margin gradient falsifies the one-reason core of whichever target theory is otherwise supported.

SIGNATURE 4 — NOISE-REGIME DISPERSION (secondary): on the no-leak cells the advocated's wide (beta, epsilon) ranges produce a between-subject SD of follow rates ~0.06-0.10, while the competing's frozen discipline ([0.80,1.00]x[0.28,0.42]x[0.12,0.16]) produces ~0.02 true SD (observed ~binomial floor). The between-subject dispersion of T9/T11/T13/T15 follow rates separately tests the two noise regimes.

HONESTY NOTE: single-cell population intervals overlap (the advocated's p_f reaches 0.84; the competing's leak-cell floor is 0.633), so no single cell is decisive; the decisive statistics are the within-subject paired contrasts (Signatures 1-2), the 16-cell profile shape, and the dispersion test — all robust to fitting beta, epsilon, gamma, sigma_h, kappa, zeta, rho_leak, boost, and tie_break to each theory (gamma, sigma_h, kappa, zeta, and tie_break are provably inert in this design: distortion is gated off, and no tilt can flip a 0.25 validity gap). The test is genuinely two-sided: a flat follow profile falsifies the competing's forced q >= 0.120 leak; a dip >= 0.05 falsifies the advocated's leak-free flatness claim. 16 unique pairs, K = 6 (96 trials exactly), give 6 repetitions per cell for stable per-subject choice proportions.

metric.metric_source:
def metric(data: pd.DataFrame) -> float:
    # THE LEAK-DIP METRIC
    # --------------------
    # Core contrast: within-subject difference between the anti-validity
    # decider-follow rate on LEAK-ELIGIBLE trials (interior-validity
    # carrier opposed by the top-validity expert) and on CONTROL trials
    # (every other trial with a discriminating carrier).
    #
    # Fixed design: validities [0.5, 0.5, 0.75, 0.75, 1.0, 1.0], ascending
    # with display index, so the anti-validity consultation order is the
    # index order (ties are inert: tied cues never oppose in any trial).
    #
    # Advocated theory: follow probability is p_f on EVERY discriminating
    # trial regardless of carrier validity, position, margin, or coalition
    #   -> expected dip = EXACTLY 0.
    # Competing theory: on the 8 leak cells the trial-conditional
    # validity-respecting leak mixes q = min(rho_leak*0.956*0.25, 0.18)
    # (>= 0.120 forced in this design) toward the TTB winner, giving
    # follow = (1-q)*p_f + q*(1-p_f) there, while control cells stay at p_f
    #   -> expected dip = -q*(2*p_f - 1) in [-0.093, -0.050], bounded away
    #      from zero by the competing's own gate formulas.
    #
    # Works on a single subject's slice (48 leak + 42 control trials) and
    # on the pooled frame alike.

    VALIDITIES = [0.5, 0.5, 0.75, 0.75, 1.0, 1.0]
    n = len(VALIDITIES)
    vmin = min(VALIDITIES)
    vmax = max(VALIDITIES)

    def to_vec(x):
        if isinstance(x, str):
            return [int(ch) for ch in x if ch in "01"]
        return [int(v) for v in x]

    # anti-validity order: ascending validity (exact ties anchor; tied cues
    # never oppose in this design, so within-tie order is inert)
    order_anti = sorted(range(n), key=lambda j: VALIDITIES[j])
    # standard TTB order: descending validity
    order_ttb = sorted(range(n), key=lambda j: -VALIDITIES[j])

    leak_follows = []
    ctrl_follows = []

    a_col = data["option_a_ratings"].tolist()
    b_col = data["option_b_ratings"].tolist()
    r_col = data["response"].tolist()

    for a_raw, b_raw, resp in zip(a_col, b_col, r_col):
        a = to_vec(a_raw)
        b = to_vec(b_raw)
        if len(a) != n or len(b) != n:
            return 0.0

        # anti-validity decider: first strictly discriminating cue in
        # ascending-validity order
        carrier = None
        favored = None
        for j in order_anti:
            if a[j] != b[j]:
                carrier = j
                favored = 0 if a[j] > b[j] else 1
                break
        if carrier is None:
            # full-tie trial (T16): no decider, excluded
            continue

        # TTB decider: first strictly discriminating cue in
        # descending-validity order
        winner_ttb = None
        for j in order_ttb:
            if a[j] != b[j]:
                winner_ttb = 0 if a[j] > b[j] else 1
                break

        # leak-eligible cell: strictly INTERIOR carrier validity
        # (min + 0.10 < val < max - 0.10) AND the TTB winner exists and
        # OPPOSES the anti-validity winner. This is exactly the
        # competing theory's trial-conditional gate; the advocated theory
        # has no mechanism tied to this conjunction.
        interior = (vmin + 0.10) < VALIDITIES[carrier] < (vmax - 0.10)
        opposed = (winner_ttb is not None) and (winner_ttb != favored)

        follow = (int(resp) == favored)
        if interior and opposed:
            leak_follows.append(follow)
        else:
            ctrl_follows.append(follow)

    if not leak_follows or not ctrl_follows:
        return 0.0

    dip = float(np.mean(leak_follows)) - float(np.mean(ctrl_follows))
    return dip
metric.rationale: THE METRIC IS THE WITHIN-SUBJECT 'LEAK DIP'. For every trial I reconstruct the anti-validity decider (first strictly discriminating cue in ascending-validity order; validities [0.5,0.5,0.75,0.75,1,1] ascend with index and tied cues never oppose, so the reconstruction is exact and tie_break/gamma inert). A trial is LEAK-ELIGIBLE iff the carrier is strictly interior (0.75) AND the standard TTB decider (descending validity) picks the opposite option — exactly the competing theory's trial-conditional gate (trials 1-8, 48 trials/subject). All other discriminating trials are CONTROLS (trials 9-15, 42 trials/subject); trial 16 (full tie) is excluded. The metric is P(follow anti-decider | leak cells) - P(follow anti-decider | control cells), computed within subject, so each subject's own p_f cancels. PREDICTIONS: the advocated theory's follow probability is flat p_f on every discriminating trial (no mechanism depends on carrier validity, position, margin, or coalition), so its dip is exactly 0 in expectation, with only binomial noise (per-subject SD ~ sqrt(p_f(1-p_f)(1/48+1/42)) ~ 0.095, giving between-subject variance ~0.009). The competing theory is FORCED by its own gate formulas to leak q = min(rho_leak*0.956*0.25, 0.18) >= 0.120 on the leak cells (its follow there is (1-q)p_f + q(1-p_f)), producing a dip of -q(2p_f-1) in [-0.093, -0.050] (mean ~ -0.08 since q saturates at 0.18 for ~90% of rho_leak's range and p_f in [0.71, 0.75]). The control cells are matched on decider validity (T9/T10/T15 are interior-carrier cells where TTB concurs) and on opposition presence (T11-T14 keep the higher-validity opposition but demote the carrier to 0.5, where the competing's gate switches the leak OFF), so both theories predict p_f there — the contrast isolates the trial-conditional leak as the sole source of any dip. Expected Welch t at N=25: gap ~0.08 against per-subject SD ~0.095 in both conditions (binomial floor dominates both theories, so between-subject variances are nearly equal at ~0.009), giving t ~ 3.0, p ~ 0.004 < alpha = 0.01. The metric is well-defined on a single subject's slice (48 leak + 42 control trials) and on the pooled frame, and it is two-sided-falsifiable: a population dip reliably below -0.05 refutes the advocated's flatness claim; a dip indistinguishable from 0 refutes the competing's forced q >= 0.120 leak.

proposer_theory.description: Anti-Validity Frugality with Diffuse Positional-Salience Heterogeneity (momentary-diffusion variant). People are one-reason decision makers: cues are consulted one at a time in descending subjective weight and the first strictly discriminating cue decides; no integration across cues (flat psychometric profile over tally margins). The population-central hierarchy is anti-validity (distrust-the-weakest, w = -validity). Each subject's weights are a continuous perturbation, w_j = -val_j + gamma*salience_j + A^3*(sigma_h*zeta_j + kappa*xi_j), where (i) salience_j is a positional gradient favoring early-listed experts with gamma drawn asymmetrically from [-0.05, +0.12] — a graded tilt, never a discrete primacy rule, bounded so it can flip nothing on the anchored designs that pin the anti-validity core; (ii) binding ambiguity A = 1 - |Spearman(position, validity)| enters CUBED, a steeply convex, gate-free gradient; and (iii) the idiosyncratic distortion is split into a small stable part (zeta_j, fixed per subject) and a large MOMENTARY part (xi_j, re-drawn every trial): under high binding ambiguity the consultation order is not merely idiosyncratic but diffuse — attention fluctuates from trial to trial, which keeps populations tight around chance-level conformity instead of spreading subjects into fixed opposing deciders. All distortion applies only when all advertised validities are distinct (exact ties anchor the distrust order). Noise is softmax(beta) over the binary winner score plus an independent lapse epsilon (implied follow p_f mean ~0.71, SD ~0.08); no discriminating cue yields exactly 0.5; validity ties are broken by a free per-subject tie-break (~80% early position); history is ignored.
proposer_theory.predict_source:
def predict(parameters, state, history):
    # Anti-Validity Frugality with Diffuse Positional-Salience Heterogeneity
    # (momentary-diffusion variant).
    #
    # One-reason decision making: cues are consulted one at a time in
    # DESCENDING subjective weight and the first strictly discriminating
    # cue decides; no integration across cues (flat psychometric profile
    # over tally margins).
    #
    # Subjective weights (continuous, per subject):
    #     w_j = -val_j + gamma * salience_j
    #            + A^3 * (sigma_h * zeta_j + kappa * xi_j)
    #
    # - ANTI-VALIDITY CORE: -val_j (distrust the weakest advertised
    #   expert; consult ascending validity).
    # - POSITIONAL SALIENCE: salience_j = (n-1-j)/(n-1) - 1/2, favoring
    #   early-listed experts; gamma is drawn ASYMMETRICALLY from
    #   [-0.05, +0.12]: the negative clamp sits above the anchored-design
    #   flip threshold (-0.0625) and the positive cap below the primacy
    #   type threshold (+0.144), so the tilt remains a graded perturbation
    #   that can never manufacture spurious pure types while retaining a
    #   partial early-position lean on anchored designs.
    # - BINDING AMBIGUITY: A = 1 - |Spearman(display position, validity)|,
    #   now entering CUBED. The steeply convex gradient keeps
    #   low/moderate-ambiguity designs anchored (A^3 ~ 0.01-0.02) while
    #   fully diffusing high-ambiguity all-distinct designs (A^3 ~ 0.3-0.6).
    # - DIFFUSE HETEROGENEITY: the idiosyncratic distortion is split into
    #   (a) a SMALL STABLE part, sigma_h * zeta_j (zeta fixed per subject,
    #   zero-centered), and (b) a LARGE MOMENTARY part, kappa * xi_j,
    #   where xi is RE-DRAWN EVERY TRIAL. Momentary consultation diffusion
    #   is what makes high-ambiguity populations tight around chance-level
    #   conformity: with fixed per-subject orders, scrambling MAXIMIZES
    #   between-subject follow-rate dispersion, whereas the observed
    #   population SD (~0.064 on the conformity-dispersion experiment)
    #   sits barely above the binomial floor. Both parts are applied ONLY
    #   when all advertised validities are distinct (exact ties anchor the
    #   distrust order).
    # NO reversal re-encoding, NO sigmoid gates, NO discrete component
    # draws.
    #
    # Noise: softmax(beta) over the binary winner score mixed with an
    # independent lapse epsilon (implied follow probability
    # p_f = (1-eps)*sigmoid(beta) + eps/2, mean ~0.71, SD ~0.08).
    # No discriminating cue -> exactly 0.5. History is ignored.
    stim = np.asarray(state, dtype=float)
    if stim.ndim != 2 or stim.shape[0] != 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Expects a (2, n_features) stimulus; got shape {stim.shape}."
        )
    n_features = stim.shape[1]

    val = np.asarray(parameters["validities"], dtype=float).ravel()
    if val.shape[0] != n_features:
        raise ValueError(
            f"validities length {val.shape[0]} != n_features {n_features}."
        )

    beta = float(parameters["beta"])
    epsilon = float(parameters["epsilon"])
    gamma = float(parameters["gamma"])
    sigma_h = float(parameters["sigma_h"])
    kappa = float(parameters["kappa"])
    tie_break = float(parameters["tie_break"])

    zeta = np.asarray(parameters["zeta"], dtype=float).ravel()
    if zeta.shape[0] != n_features:
        # NO silent zeros fallback: a shape mismatch means the entire
        # heterogeneity mechanism would be silently disabled, so fail
        # loudly instead (per the arbiter's diagnosis request).
        raise ValueError(
            f"zeta length {zeta.shape[0]} != n_features {n_features}."
        )

    # ---- helper: average-tie ranks ----
    def avg_ranks(x):
        n = x.shape[0]
        srt = np.argsort(x, kind="stable")
        ranks = np.empty(n, dtype=float)
        i = 0
        while i < n:
            j = i
            while j + 1 < n and x[srt[j + 1]] == x[srt[i]]:
                j += 1
            ranks[srt[i:j + 1]] = 0.5 * (i + j)  # 0-indexed average rank
            i = j + 1
        return ranks

    # ---- positional-salience gradient (early-listed experts favored) ----
    # Centered so the tilt is a pure graded perturbation: +0.5 at the
    # first listed expert, -0.5 at the last, linear in between.
    if n_features > 1:
        sal = ((n_features - 1 - np.arange(n_features, dtype=float))
               / (n_features - 1.0)) - 0.5
    else:
        sal = np.zeros(1, dtype=float)

    # ---- binding ambiguity: A = 1 - |Spearman(position, validity)| ----
    if n_features > 1:
        ranks = avg_ranks(val)
        pos_r = np.arange(n_features, dtype=float)
        vp = pos_r - pos_r.mean()
        vr = ranks - ranks.mean()
        denom = np.sqrt(float((vp * vp).sum()) * float((vr * vr).sum()))
        if denom > 1e-12:
            rho = float((vp * vr).sum()) / denom
        else:
            # All validities tied: distrust order undefined.
            rho = 0.0
        ambiguity = 1.0 - abs(rho)
    else:
        ambiguity = 0.0

    # ---- continuous subjective weights ----
    w = -val + gamma * sal

    # ---- diffuse idiosyncratic distortion (distinct lists only) ----
    # Exact validity ties anchor the distrust order (no distortion);
    # all-distinct lists degrade with the CUBE of binding ambiguity.
    # The distortion is split into a small STABLE per-subject part
    # (sigma_h * zeta) and a large MOMENTARY per-trial part (kappa * xi,
    # xi re-drawn fresh on every call), so that high-ambiguity designs
    # show tight, chance-centered conformity rather than fixed
    # idiosyncratic deciders that spread the population apart.
    distinct = (np.unique(val).shape[0] == n_features)
    if distinct and ambiguity > 0.0:
        amb3 = ambiguity * ambiguity * ambiguity
        xi = np.random.uniform(-1.0, 1.0, size=n_features)
        w = w + amb3 * (sigma_h * zeta + kappa * xi)

    # Consult cues in DESCENDING subjective weight. np.lexsort uses the
    # LAST key as primary. Exact ties in w are broken by the free
    # per-subject tie_break parameter (population-consistent: ~80% of
    # subjects break ties by early display position).
    pos = np.arange(n_features)
    secondary = pos if tie_break < 0.8 else (n_features - 1 - pos)
    cue_order = np.lexsort((secondary, -w))

    a, b = stim[0], stim[1]
    winner = None
    for j in cue_order:
        if a[j] > b[j]:
            winner = 0
            break
        if b[j] > a[j]:
            winner = 1
            break

    n_opts = 2
    if winner is None:
        # No discriminating cue: pure guess (lapse mixing leaves a
        # uniform unchanged).
        return np.ones(n_opts) / float(n_opts)

    scores = np.array([1.0, 0.0]) if winner == 0 else np.array([0.0, 1.0])

    # Numerically stable softmax over the binary winner score: the
    # winner's probability is sigmoid(beta). Implied decider-follow
    # probability p_f = (1-eps)*sigmoid(beta) + eps/2 has mean ~0.71
    # with per-subject SD ~0.08 over the sampled (beta, epsilon) ranges.
    z = beta * (scores - scores.max())
    e = np.exp(z)
    p_core = e / e.sum()

    return (1.0 - epsilon) * p_core + epsilon * (np.ones(n_opts) / float(n_opts))
proposer_theory.rationale: Minimal-diff edit of the ACCEPTED base (loss 0.0915), addressing the critic's (A)-(E) with one structural addition my own moment audit shows is necessary. (A) PATHWAY VERIFICATION — the critic suspects zeta is silently zeroed. It is not: a zeta-zeroed model (pure anti-validity core at this p_f regime, mean ~0.71) produces an Exp-10 index near the pi_4 level (~590), while the simulation returns 241; moreover iter-1 (weaker sigma_h, linear A) gave 255 and iter-2 (nearly doubled sigma_h, A-squared) gave 241 — a SATURATED lever, not an inert one. I did remove the silent zeros fallback (it now raises), so any future shape mismatch fails loudly. (B) THE REAL Exp-10 DIAGNOSIS — the residual +124 is carried by the dispersion term: our per-subject var is 0.0134 vs observed 0.0041. With FIXED per-subject consultation orders, scrambling MAXIMIZES between-subject follow-rate dispersion (each subject's order deterministically flips or matches each cue pair, giving between-subject SD ~0.13-0.17); the observed SD 0.064 sits barely above the binomial floor (0.053 at ~90 trials). No recalibration of a fixed zeta — including the critic's suggested sigma_h [0.6,1.2] with zeta +/-1, which by my pair-flip calculation still lands near ~200 — can produce a tight, chance-centered population. The fix: split the distortion into a small STABLE part (sigma_h*zeta, exactly the critic's suggested range) plus a large MOMENTARY per-trial diffusion (kappa*xi, fresh every trial). This keeps every pooled-mean metric identical to the fixed-zeta version (means are linear in the noise distribution) while collapsing the between-subject Gini to the binomial floor plus a small stable component. Moment math on Exp 10 (A=0.857, A^3=0.63, kappa~10 -> per-cue noise std ~3.6): mean follow ~0.505, per-subject SD ~0.06 -> index ~100-135 (observed 116.6, var ~0.004) instead of 241. On Exp 12 (A^3=0.32, noise ~1.9): analytic full-diffusion follow = 0.535 vs observed 0.532. I steepened the gradient from A^2 to A^3 so that Exp 9 (A=0.23, A^3~0.012 -> noise ~0.08, close to its current ~0.15) stays anchored at its excellent current fit (0.416 vs 0.428); a linear or quadratic scaling at Exp-10-appropriate magnitude would over-scramble Exp 9 toward 0.5. (C) Exp 4 — adopted the critic's asymmetric gamma [-0.05, +0.12] verbatim: the floor sits above the anchored-design flip threshold (-0.0625) and the cap below the Exp-14 primacy threshold (+0.144), so Exp 14 stays exactly 0.000 with var 0 and Exp 7 keeps its recovered opposition while a positive tail partially restores the early-position lean the gamma tightening removed. (D) GATE RELAXATION REJECTED, with a cell-level audit: on Exp 8 (tied, A=0.77) all four margin-0 deciders ALREADY oppose the reversed hierarchy — the model sits at the family's maximum opposition (1-p_f ~ 0.27; observed -0.289 exceeds even that), so dispersion can only wash it toward 0; on Exp 13 (tied, A=0.91) the observed 0.150 lies BELOW the pure-opposition floor 1-p_f ~ 0.29, and noise drifts the metric UP toward 0.5; on Exp 7 dispersion washes the signed contrast toward 0, the wrong direction from -0.196 vs observed -0.311. Only Exp 5 would benefit, and it cannot outweigh three regressions; I also verified the tie-break is inert on the metric cells of Exps 5, 6, 7, 11 and 13. (E) p_f untouched (mean ~0.71, SD ~0.08): Exp 3 pins it at 0.727 and the de-conformity on Exps 10/12 now comes from decider diffusion, not response weakness. Acknowledged family limits left in place: Exps 13 and 7 (observed opposition beyond 1-p_f), Exp 5 (tied-design over-conformity, unfixable without the rejected gate relaxation), Exp 1 (TTB-following level pinned near 1-p_f). Expected net movement: Exp 10 from +124 to roughly 0 +/- 20, Exp 12 from +0.037 to ~0, Exp 4 recovery toward +0.04 if the gamma mechanism is as the critic's audit indicates, with Exps 2, 3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 11, 13, 14 preserved — comfortably below the accepted loss floor.

experiment.rationale:
GOAL: Quantitatively dissociate Anchored Anti-Validity Frugality with Validity-Respecting Leak, frozen-discipline variant (advocated) from Anti-Validity Frugality with Diffuse Positional-Salience Heterogeneity, momentary-diffusion variant (competing). Both share the anti-validity one-reason core, the same A^3-gated distortion rule, and the same tie-anchoring rule, and experiment [16] already exploited the one mechanism the advocated uniquely has (the trial-conditional TTB leak) in a tied-validity, ambiguity-0.044 regime. This design occupies a different, unexplored corner: the ZERO-AMBIGUITY, ALL-DISTINCT regime in which every gated channel (momentary diffusion, stable zeta, gap-proportional anchoring, leak on weak-block deciders) is STRUCTURALLY OFF in both theories, leaving exactly one active difference: the UNGATED positional-salience tilt gamma*salience, which both theories apply unconditionally but with committed different magnitudes — the competing draws gamma asymmetrically from [-0.05, +0.12] (a real, population-level early-position lean), while the advocated's gamma is confined to [-0.01, +0.03] (effectively zero). The design converts this tilt-magnitude difference into a measurable VALIDITY-GAP PSYCHOMETRIC.

SETUP: 6 features, validities [0.95, 0.78, 0.534, 0.53, 0.52, 0.50] (f0..f5), strictly DECREASING in position, so Spearman(position, validity) = -1, binding ambiguity = 0 exactly: both theories' `distinct and ambiguity > 0` gates shut all distortion off, and all validities distinct makes tie_break inert in both. The consultation order is therefore deterministic per subject: w_j = -val_j + gamma*sal_j with sal = [+0.5, +0.3, +0.1, -0.1, -0.3, -0.5]. The anti-validity core consults f5 (50%) -> f4 (52%) -> f3 (53%) -> f2 (53.4%) -> f1 (78%) -> f0 (95%). KEY MECHANIC: for any two cues X (earlier position, higher validity) and Y (later, weaker), the subject consults X before Y iff gamma > Delta_v / Delta_sal =: g. So on a trial where ONLY X and Y discriminate in opposition, the choice reveals a threshold crossing of the subject's gamma. The weak block {f2..f5} is engineered with tiny, varied gaps so that different cue pairs realize a LADDER of thresholds g = 0.020, 0.035, 0.050, 0.057, 0.075, 0.100 — spanning the competing's gamma range while sitting (except the lowest rung) entirely ABOVE the advocated's gamma cap of 0.03.

PREDICTED FLIP RATES P(consult the earlier cue first): competing, gamma ~ Uniform[-0.05, 0.12]: P(gamma > g) = (0.12 - g)/0.17 = 0.588, 0.500, 0.412, 0.372, 0.265, 0.118 across the six rungs. Advocated, gamma ~ Uniform[-0.01, 0.03]: 0.25 at g = 0.020 and EXACTLY ZERO at every rung with g >= 0.035 — RANGE-FORCED, since gamma <= 0.03 < 0.035 for any admissible parameter setting. Population p(earlier-cue option), p_E = P_flip*p_f + (1-P_flip)*(1-p_f): competing (p_f mean 0.71) predicts 0.537, 0.500, 0.463, 0.446, 0.401, 0.340; advocated (p_f = (1-eps)*sigmoid(beta*(1+boost)*(1+b_distinct)) + eps/2 in [0.678, 0.832] at ambiguity 0 with the distinct-design bonus) predicts 0.334-0.411 at g = 0.020 and a FLAT 1 - p_f in [0.168, 0.322] on all five higher rungs.

SIGNATURE 1 — THE GAP PSYCHOMETRIC (primary): the competing predicts a strictly GRADED p_E(g), falling ~0.20 from the lowest to the highest rung (0.537 -> 0.340); the advocated predicts a FLAT profile at 1 - p_f across g = 0.035...0.100 (range-forced zero flips), with at most a single small step at g = 0.020. The paired within-subject contrast p_E(g=0.035) - p_E(g=0.100) is ~ +0.16 under the competing and EXACTLY ZERO under the advocated. Mirror pairs (T1/T2, T3/T4, T5/T6, T9/T10) cancel side bias; p_E is pooled over each mirror pair (12 trials/subject per rung).

SIGNATURE 2 — THE MIDPOINT KNIFE EDGE (T3/T4, g = 0.035, the exact midpoint of the competing's gamma interval): the competing predicts p_E = 0.500 EXACTLY, for ANY (beta, epsilon) — with P_flip = 0.5, p_E = 0.5*p_f + 0.5*(1-p_f) = 0.5, a parameter-free point prediction. The advocated is range-forced to p_E = 1 - p_f <= 0.322. The intervals [0.500] and [0.168, 0.322] are DISJOINT: population p_E > 0.42 on this rung falsifies the advocated at any parameter setting; p_E < 0.40 falsifies the competing's asymmetric-tilt prior.

SIGNATURE 3 — PER-SUBJECT STEP FUNCTION AND DISPERSION (sharpest structural test): each competing subject holds ONE gamma, so choices across the six rungs trace a STEP FUNCTION in g (follow the earlier cue on rungs below gamma-hat, the weaker cue above it); ~50% of subjects have gamma-hat inside (0.035, 0.12] and thus flip somewhere on the ladder, and at g = 0.035 the population is BIMODAL (half at p_f ~ 0.71, half at 1 - p_f ~ 0.29; between-subject SD ~ 0.21). The advocated predicts ZERO subjects flip on any g >= 0.035 rung — every subject follows the weaker cue, tight cluster at 1 - p_f (true SD ~ 0.03-0.04). A single subject following the earlier cue consistently (beyond binomial noise, P ~ 0.09 per 6-rep cell at worst-case p_f) on any g >= 0.035 cell falsifies the advocated outright; a near-unimodal low cluster falsifies the competing's committed gamma distribution. The design thus MEASURES the population gamma distribution directly, making the competing's prior-based commitment empirically testable rather than assumable.

SIGNATURE 4 — THE ADVOCATED'S OWN GAMMA CAP (T1/T2, g = 0.020): the advocated predicts a 25% flip rate there (p_E ~ 0.375), the competing 58.8% (p_E ~ 0.537) — disjoint intervals [0.334, 0.411] vs [0.50, 0.57], a genuinely two-sided test of each theory's tilt prior at its left end.

SIGNATURE 5 — SECONDARY LEAK PROBE (C3 vs C4): C3 pits the interior-validity 78% expert (the stable anti-decider, j* interior since 0.60 < 0.78 < 0.85) against the 95% expert in opposition; the advocated's trial-conditional leak fires with q = min(rho_leak * 1.00 * 0.090, 0.18) in [0.045, 0.18] (forced by rho_leak >= 0.5, coherence = 1, mean_gap = 0.090), predicting a within-subject dip q*(2*p_f - 1) in [0.016, 0.120] relative to the matched concordance cell C4 (same decider, TTB opposition removed, no mixture). The competing predicts EXACTLY ZERO dip. This axis is weak here by construction (the tilt design requires tiny gaps, which shrink mean_gap), so it is secondary; [16] tested the leak at full strength. All tilt-cell and control-cell deciders are weak-block or min/max-validity cues, so the leak is provably OFF on T1-T10, C1, C2, C5 — the tilt signatures are uncontaminated.

SIGNATURE 6 — CONTROLS: C1/C5 (lone weakest / lone block decider) are agreement cells pinning p_f for both theories and separating the noise regimes (advocated frozen-narrow p_f in [0.678, 0.832], between-subject SD ~ 0.03; competing p_f in [0.51, 0.92], SD ~ 0.08). C2 (weakest 50% expert vs the 95% expert, in opposition) tests the SHARED anti-validity core: both theories follow the 50% expert at p_f; if subjects instead follow the 95% expert, both target theories fail together. C6 (full tie) pins both to exactly 0.50, anchoring lapse and side bias.

HONESTY NOTES: (i) Within every critical pair the earlier-position cue is also the higher-validity cue — unavoidable, since zero ambiguity (Spearman = -1) forces position-validity alignment; a pure validity-respecting strategist would also produce the competing's tilt-side predictions, so elevated p_E falsifies the advocated without uniquely confirming the competing (C2 partially guards the shared anti-validity core). (ii) The competing's flip commitment is prior-based (its asymmetric gamma draw), not range-forced: a post-hoc refit with gamma ~ 0 for every subject could mimic the flat profile, but only by contradicting the competing's own stated population prior (mean +0.035, 41% of subjects above 0.05, 50% above 0.035) — the ladder measures that distribution directly, so the concession would be visible and quantified. (iii) Single-cell intervals overlap at the high-g rungs (g = 0.075, 0.100); the decisive evidence is the low-g rungs, the psychometric slope, and the per-subject step/dispersion structure — all robust to fitting beta, epsilon, gamma, sigma_h, kappa, zeta, rho_leak, boost, b_distinct, and tie_break to each theory (sigma_h, kappa, zeta, tie_break are provably inert at ambiguity 0 with distinct validities). (iv) The g = 0.035 knife edge assumes the competing's gamma draw is uniform on [-0.05, +0.12]; under any prior with appreciable mass in the upper half of that interval the prediction remains well above the advocated's forced ceiling. With 16 unique pairs and K = 6 (96 trials exactly), each cell yields 6 repetitions per subject for stable choice proportions.

metric.metric_source:
def metric(data: pd.DataFrame) -> float:
    # TAIL HETEROGENEITY OF ANTI-VALIDITY DECIDER-FOLLOW RATES.
    #
    # Stage 1 (per subject): estimate the subject's decider-follow rate
    #   p_hat over all non-tie trials. The decider on each trial is the
    #   first discriminating expert in the subject's anti-validity
    #   consultation order: weakest advertised validity first; within the
    #   tied 0.5 block the order is positional, with the side
    #   (earlier-position-first vs later-position-first) inferred from the
    #   subject's own weak-block choices (reliable: the per-subject
    #   earlier-follow rate sits near 0.73 or 0.27 across the 60
    #   weak-block trials).
    # Stage 2 (population): the metric is the mean of the largest 20% of
    #   per-subject absolute deviations |p_hat - 0.72|, i.e. the TAIL
    #   dispersion of response discipline across subjects.
    #
    # The advocated theory's frozen parameter windows confine every
    #   subject's follow probability to [0.67, 0.78] (population SD
    #   ~0.015), so its deviation tail is set by the binomial sampling
    #   floor alone (~0.09). The competing theory samples beta over
    #   [0.5, 1.9] and epsilon over [0.08, 0.24], implying per-subject
    #   follow rates spanning [0.59, 0.84] with SD ~0.07, which lifts the
    #   tail to ~0.16.
    VALS = (0.95, 0.78, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5)
    CENTER = 0.72
    TAIL_FRAC = 0.2

    def parse_ratings(x):
        if isinstance(x, str):
            x = x.strip().strip("[]").split(",")
        try:
            items = list(x)
        except TypeError:
            return None
        out = []
        for v in items:
            try:
                out.append(int(round(float(v))))
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                return None
        return out if len(out) == 6 else None

    per_subject = {}
    for sid, a_raw, b_raw, r_raw in zip(
        data["subject_id"],
        data["option_a_ratings"],
        data["option_b_ratings"],
        data["response"],
    ):
        a = parse_ratings(a_raw)
        b = parse_ratings(b_raw)
        if a is None or b is None:
            continue
        try:
            r = int(r_raw)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            continue
        per_subject.setdefault(sid, []).append((a, b, r))

    devs = []
    for trials in per_subject.values():
        # --- infer the subject's weak-block positional side ---
        early_follows = []
        for a, b, r in trials:
            disc = [j for j in range(6) if a[j] != b[j]]
            if len(disc) == 2 and disc[0] >= 2:
                j1 = disc[0]
                endorsed_early = 0 if a[j1] == 1 else 1
                early_follows.append(1 if r == endorsed_early else 0)
        early_side = (
            len(early_follows) > 0
            and 2 * sum(early_follows) > len(early_follows)
        )

        # --- decider-follow rate over all non-tie trials ---
        follows = []
        for a, b, r in trials:
            disc = [j for j in range(6) if a[j] != b[j]]
            if not disc:
                continue  # full tie: no decider, no information
            if early_side:
                j_star = min(disc, key=lambda j: (VALS[j], j))
            else:
                j_star = min(disc, key=lambda j: (VALS[j], -j))
            endorsed = 0 if a[j_star] == 1 else 1
            follows.append(1 if r == endorsed else 0)

        if not follows:
            continue
        p_hat = float(sum(follows)) / float(len(follows))
        devs.append(abs(p_hat - CENTER))

    if not devs:
        return 0.0
    devs = sorted(devs, reverse=True)
    k = max(1, int(np.ceil(TAIL_FRAC * len(devs))))
    return float(sum(devs[:k]) / float(k))
metric.rationale:
WHY THE PREVIOUS METRIC FAILED AND WHAT SURVIVES. With this experiment's actual validities [0.95, 0.78, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5], the weak block is EXACTLY TIED, so `distinct` is False in both theories' predict functions: every gated distortion channel (momentary diffusion, stable zeta, gap-proportional anchoring, distinct-design bonus) is structurally OFF in BOTH theories. Both reduce to the same deterministic anti-validity cascade whose weak-block consultation order is set purely by the SIGN of the positional tilt gamma, plus a subject-level decider-follow probability p_f = (1-eps)*sigmoid(beta_eff) + eps/2. The failed tilt metric showed the gamma-sign weights are nearly identical across theories (advocated 0.75, competing ~0.8), so the tilt axis is dead. The one large population-level difference that survives is RESPONSE-DISCIPLINE DISPERSION — the very 'frozen-discipline vs diffuse-heterogeneity' contrast defining the two theories. Advocated: beta in [0.8,1.0], boost in [0.28,0.42], epsilon in [0.12,0.16] give beta_eff in [0.99,1.35] and p_f confined to [0.67,0.78] with population SD ~0.015. Competing: beta in [0.5,1.9] and epsilon in [0.08,0.24] give p_f spanning [0.59,0.84] with SD ~0.07 — a 4-5x dispersion ratio.

METRIC CONSTRUCTION. (1) Per subject, infer the weak-block positional side behaviorally (follow-earlier rate over the 60 weak-block trials is ~0.73 or ~0.27, so classification is essentially error-free and even handles gamma=0 tie-break subjects correctly). (2) Label every non-tie trial's decider as the weakest-validity discriminating expert (weak-block ties resolved by the inferred side) and compute the subject's decider-follow rate p_hat over the 90 informative trials. (3) The metric is the mean of the largest 20% of per-subject |p_hat - 0.72| values — the tail of the discipline distribution. The tail is used because the theories differ most there: the advocated HARD-BOUNDS every subject's p_f into [0.67,0.78] (its tail is pure binomial noise), while the competing regularly manufactures extreme followers (p_f near 0.6 or 0.84); a plain mean of deviations would be diluted by the shared binomial floor. Averaging the top quintile (rather than taking a maximum) keeps the statistic stable against single-subject binomial flukes.

PREDICTIONS. Advocated: p_hat ~ N(0.726, 0.049), top-quintile mean deviation ~0.09 (range 0.08-0.11). Competing: p_hat ~ N(0.73, 0.085), top-quintile mean ~0.16 (range 0.13-0.19). The per-subject statistic |p_hat-0.72| is tight (SD ~0.03 advocated, ~0.05 competing), so the between-subject variance is small while the pooled gap is ~0.07 — a Welch t well above threshold at N=25. The contrast is robust: it persists even if the competing's effective p_f SD is as low as 0.04, it is insensitive to the tilt-sign similarity that killed the previous metric, it uses all 90 informative trials per subject, mirror pairs cancel side bias, and the formula is well-defined on any subset (a single-subject slice returns that subject's own deviation), so the per-subject reapplication needed for the between-subject variance is valid. It also cleanly separates the shared anti-validity core (used to identify deciders) from the discipline dispersion being measured, so it is not trivially satisfied by either theory's cascade structure.

proposer_theory.description: Anchored Anti-Validity Frugality with Validity-Respecting Leak (frozen-discipline variant). People are one-reason decision makers: experts are consulted one at a time and the first strictly discriminating expert decides; no integration across cues. The population-central hierarchy is anti-validity (distrust-the-weakest) and the population is typeless — every subject is a continuous perturbation around that core. Three graded, design-scaled mechanisms modulate the core. (1) GAP-PROPORTIONAL ANCHORING: per-trial attention noise on expert j is scaled by the local validity gaps adjacent to j in the subjective order, gated by cubed binding ambiguity, so validity-isolated experts anchor the order while dense clusters diffuse; exact validity ties anchor the order entirely. (2) VALIDITY-RESPECTING LEAK, now TRIAL-CONDITIONAL and implemented as a probability mixture: the leak toward the standard TTB (descending-validity) order fires only when the anti-validity cascade's first discriminating expert on that trial is a strictly INTERIOR validity (min_val + 0.10 < val < max_val - 0.10), with design-level probability q = min(rho_leak * reversal_coherence * mean_gap, 0.18). When the anti-decider's carrier is a weakest or near-top expert, the leak is switched off — protecting the pure anti-validity-follow designs — while genuinely mid-validity carriers let a fraction of trials flip toward the strongest discriminator, generating below-chance reversed-cascade following where the data demand it. (3) DESIGN-SCALED RESPONSE DISCIPLINE with a DISTINCT-DESIGN BONUS: p_f = (1-eps)*sigmoid(beta_eff) + eps/2 with beta_eff = beta*(1 + boost*(1-A))*(1 + b_distinct) when all validities are distinct — distinct-validity designs (which the data show want tighter decider-following) get a bounded bonus, tie designs are untouched. Response-discipline and diffusion parameters are FROZEN at narrow windows reproducing the accepted base's behavior, so only the leak strength and the distinct bonus are free.
proposer_theory.predict_source:
def predict(parameters, state, history):
    # Anchored Anti-Validity Frugality with Validity-Respecting Leak
    # (frozen-discipline variant).
    #
    # Minimal-diff edit of the accepted iter-1 base:
    #   (a) The validity-respecting leak is now TRIAL-CONDITIONAL: it is
    #       eligible only when the anti-validity cascade's first
    #       discriminating expert j* on this trial carries a strictly
    #       INTERIOR validity (min + 0.10 < val[j*] < max - 0.10), and
    #       it is implemented as a PROBABILITY MIXTURE (no Bernoulli
    #       draw) with ceiling 0.18.
    #   (b) A DISTINCT-DESIGN BONUS b_distinct multiplies beta_eff when
    #       all validities are distinct (tie designs untouched).
    #   (c) Response-discipline / diffusion parameters are FROZEN at
    #       narrow windows that reproduce the accepted base's behavior;
    #       only rho_leak and b_distinct are genuinely free.
    stim = np.asarray(state, dtype=float)
    if stim.ndim != 2 or stim.shape[0] != 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Expects a (2, n_features) stimulus; got shape {stim.shape}."
        )
    n_features = stim.shape[1]

    val = np.asarray(parameters["validities"], dtype=float).ravel()
    if val.shape[0] != n_features:
        raise ValueError(
            f"validities length {val.shape[0]} != n_features {n_features}."
        )

    beta = float(parameters["beta"])
    boost = float(parameters["boost"])
    b_distinct = float(parameters["b_distinct"])
    epsilon = float(parameters["epsilon"])
    gamma = float(parameters["gamma"])
    kappa = float(parameters["kappa"])
    sigma_h = float(parameters["sigma_h"])
    rho_leak = float(parameters["rho_leak"])
    tie_break = float(parameters["tie_break"])

    zeta = np.asarray(parameters["zeta"], dtype=float).ravel()
    if zeta.shape[0] != n_features:
        raise ValueError(
            f"zeta length {zeta.shape[0]} != n_features {n_features}."
        )

    # ---- helper: average-tie ranks ----
    def avg_ranks(x):
        n = x.shape[0]
        srt = np.argsort(x, kind="stable")
        ranks = np.empty(n, dtype=float)
        i = 0
        while i < n:
            j = i
            while j + 1 < n and x[srt[j + 1]] == x[srt[i]]:
                j += 1
            ranks[srt[i:j + 1]] = 0.5 * (i + j)  # 0-indexed average rank
            i = j + 1
        return ranks

    # ---- positional-salience gradient (early-listed experts favored) ----
    if n_features > 1:
        sal = ((n_features - 1 - np.arange(n_features, dtype=float))
               / (n_features - 1.0)) - 0.5
    else:
        sal = np.zeros(1, dtype=float)

    # ---- binding ambiguity: A = 1 - |Spearman(position, validity)| ----
    if n_features > 1:
        ranks = avg_ranks(val)
        pos_r = np.arange(n_features, dtype=float)
        vp = pos_r - pos_r.mean()
        vr = ranks - ranks.mean()
        denom = np.sqrt(float((vp * vp).sum()) * float((vr * vr).sum()))
        if denom > 1e-12:
            rho = float((vp * vr).sum()) / denom
        else:
            rho = 0.0
        ambiguity = 1.0 - abs(rho)
    else:
        ambiguity = 0.0

    # ---- reversal coherence: |Spearman(validity, validity[::-1])| ----
    if n_features > 1:
        ranks_v = avg_ranks(val)
        ranks_r = avg_ranks(val[::-1])
        dv = ranks_v - ranks_v.mean()
        dr = ranks_r - ranks_r.mean()
        denom2 = np.sqrt(float((dv * dv).sum()) * float((dr * dr).sum()))
        if denom2 > 1e-12:
            rho_rev = float((dv * dr).sum()) / denom2
        else:
            rho_rev = 0.0
        coherence = abs(rho_rev)
    else:
        coherence = 0.0

    # ---- mean adjacent validity gap over UNIQUE validities ----
    uvals = np.unique(val)
    if uvals.size > 1:
        mean_gap = float(np.mean(np.diff(np.sort(uvals))))
    else:
        mean_gap = 0.0

    distinct = (uvals.size == n_features)

    # ---- gap-proportional anchoring ratios (verbatim from base) ----
    ref_gap = 0.10
    gap_ratio = np.ones(n_features, dtype=float)
    if distinct and n_features > 1:
        srt = np.argsort(val, kind="stable")
        sv = val[srt]
        gs = np.ones(n_features, dtype=float)
        for r in range(n_features):
            g = 0.0
            if r > 0:
                g += sv[r] - sv[r - 1]          # gap to next weaker
            if r < n_features - 1:
                g += sv[r + 1] - sv[r]          # gap to next stronger
            gs[srt[r]] = max(g, 0.05)           # numerical floor
        gap_ratio = np.minimum(ref_gap / gs, 2.0)

    amb3 = ambiguity * ambiguity * ambiguity

    pos = np.arange(n_features)
    secondary = pos if tie_break < 0.8 else (n_features - 1 - pos)

    a, b = stim[0], stim[1]

    def cascade_winner(order):
        for j in order:
            if a[j] > b[j]:
                return 0
            if b[j] > a[j]:
                return 1
        return None

    # ---- STABLE anti-validity weights (no momentary noise): used ONLY
    # to locate this trial's anti-validity carrier j* for the leak gate.
    w_stable = -val + gamma * sal
    if distinct and ambiguity > 0.0:
        w_stable = w_stable + amb3 * kappa * gap_ratio * sigma_h * zeta
    order_stable = np.lexsort((secondary, -w_stable))

    j_star = None
    for j in order_stable:
        if a[j] != b[j]:
            j_star = int(j)
            break

    # ---- TRIAL-CONDITIONAL leak eligibility: strictly interior carrier.
    # Weakest-expert carriers (val <= min + 0.10) and near-top carriers
    # (val >= max - 0.10) switch the leak OFF; only genuinely mid-
    # validity carriers let the TTB leak fire. Ceiling 0.18.
    leak_q = 0.0
    if j_star is not None and n_features > 1:
        vmin = float(val.min())
        vmax = float(val.max())
        if (vmin + 0.10) < val[j_star] < (vmax - 0.10):
            leak_q = float(min(rho_leak * coherence * mean_gap, 0.18))

    # ---- per-trial subjective hierarchy (momentary diffusion added) ----
    w = w_stable.copy()
    if distinct and ambiguity > 0.0:
        xi = np.random.normal(0.0, 1.0, size=n_features)
        w = w + amb3 * kappa * gap_ratio * xi
    order_anti = np.lexsort((secondary, -w))
    winner_anti = cascade_winner(order_anti)

    n_opts = 2
    if winner_anti is None:
        # No discriminating cue: pure guess (lapse mixing leaves a
        # uniform unchanged).
        return np.ones(n_opts) / float(n_opts)

    # ---- design-scaled response discipline with DISTINCT-DESIGN BONUS ----
    beta_eff = beta * (1.0 + boost * (1.0 - ambiguity))
    if distinct:
        beta_eff = beta_eff * (1.0 + b_distinct)

    def score_prob(winner):
        scores = np.array([1.0, 0.0]) if winner == 0 else np.array([0.0, 1.0])
        z = beta_eff * (scores - scores.max())
        e = np.exp(z)
        return e / e.sum()

    p_core = score_prob(winner_anti)

    # ---- VALIDITY-RESPECTING LEAK as a probability mixture (no
    # Bernoulli draw -> lower Monte Carlo variance in simulated metrics).
    if leak_q > 0.0:
        order_ttb = np.lexsort((secondary, -val))
        winner_ttb = cascade_winner(order_ttb)
        if winner_ttb is not None and winner_ttb != winner_anti:
            p_core = (1.0 - leak_q) * p_core + leak_q * score_prob(winner_ttb)

    return (1.0 - epsilon) * p_core + epsilon * (np.ones(n_opts) / float(n_opts))
proposer_theory.rationale: This is a surgical edit of the accepted iter-1 base implementing the iter-3 critic's prescription, whose two prior rejection diagnoses I take as ground truth: (i) the leak-gate DIRECTION was empirically right both times (Exps 3/9/10 moved correctly in isolation), but (ii) range-narrowing failed twice as a drift-control strategy because the leak changed the joint likelihood landscape and dragged the shared response-discipline parameters (beta/boost) upward, inflating p_f and regressing every decider-follow metric (Exps 4, 5, 6, 10, 7, 13). I therefore change the drift-control STRATEGY, not just the ranges. (1) FREEZE: beta, boost, epsilon, gamma, kappa, sigma_h are confined to narrow windows centered on the base's mid-range values (I verified analytically that mid-range values reproduce the base's Exp-5 follow of ~0.68 and Exp-3 anti-follow of ~0.71, i.e., the base's operating point), so only rho_leak and the new b_distinct are effectively free. (2) SYMMETRIC INTERIOR GATE (delta = 0.10 hardcoded): the leak is eligible only when the anti-validity cascade's carrier j* on this trial satisfies min + 0.10 < val[j*] < max - 0.10. Hand-traced consequences: on Exp 3 the carrier is always the 0.5-validity minimum expert -> leak provably OFF -> Exp 3 must stay at (or slightly above, via the distinct bonus) the base's value, serving as the freeze regression test; on Exp 6 the carriers are the 0.6-validity minima -> leak OFF; on Exp 7 the design's validity set {0.6, 0.65, 0.85, 0.9, 0.95} contains NO strictly interior values, so the leak never fires there — this removes iter-2's wrong-direction T11 flip while restoring the base's pure anti-follow; on Exp 9 the dissociating carriers are weak experts (<= 0.7 = min + 0.10) -> leak OFF, protecting the near-exact 0.427 fit; on Exp 8 the interior carriers (0.75, 0.8) let the leak flip toward TTB exactly where TTB opposes the reversed cascade, pushing the metric more negative as the data demand. (3) PROBABILITY MIXTURE instead of a per-trial Bernoulli for the leak (numerically equivalent, lower Monte Carlo variance), with ceiling lowered to 0.18 and rho_leak widened to [0.5, 3.0] so the cap — not an attenuated coherence x gap product — does the bounding on high-product designs (Exp 13's product is ~0.097, so the leak can reach the cap there if the fit wants it). (4) DISTINCT-DESIGN BONUS b_distinct in [0, 0.25] multiplying beta_eff when all validities are distinct: this is the orthogonal p_f knob the critic prescribed, along the axis (distinct vs tied) the data actually support — it raises follow on the distinct designs that undershoot (Exps 1, 3, 10, 15) while leaving the tie designs (Exps 5, 6, 7, 13) exactly at base behavior, preventing the cross-contamination that killed iters 2 and 3. (5) Exp 10 is the top-priority target (largest base miss, -31): the interior gate switches the leak off on its weakest-carrier agreeing cells, and the bounded distinct bonus raises the mean follow toward the real level without the uncontrolled inflation that overshot iter-3 to 150.9. I accept Exp 13 (~0.30 vs 0.15) and the Exp 7 structural cap (~-0.20 vs -0.31) as residual misses shared by every one-reason competitor, per the critic's explicit instruction not to trade the winnable experiments for them. All changes stay strictly inside the prescribed Anchored Anti-Validity Frugality with Validity-Respecting Leak family.

next_theory.description: Diffuse Mixture Frugality with Strong Interior-Gated Validity Leak (sub-linear coherence variant). People are one-reason decision makers: experts are consulted one at a time and the first strictly discriminating expert decides; no integration across cues, no history use, exact validity ties anchor the consultation order, and a trial with no discriminating expert yields exactly 0.5. The population-central hierarchy is anti-validity (distrust-the-weakest: consult ascending advertised validity). Three graded mechanisms modulate the core. (1) STRONG INTERIOR-GATED VALIDITY LEAK with SUB-LINEAR COHERENCE WEIGHTING: when the anti cascade's first discriminating expert carries a strictly interior validity (min + 0.10 < val < max - 0.10), the decision mixes toward the standard TTB (descending-validity) decider with probability q = rho_leak * sqrt(reversal_coherence) * gap_term, where gap_term is the range-normalized mean adjacent unique-validity gap. The sub-linear coherence exponent leaves fully reversal-coherent designs (coherence ~ 1) exactly on their calibrated anchor values while granting moderately coherent designs substantially more leak mass than the linear weighting did — capturing the empirical fact that leak toward the strongest expert is not confined to perfectly mirror-structured validity lists. (2) DIFFUSE HETEROGENEITY: w_j = -val_j + gamma*salience_j + A^3*(sigma_h*zeta_j + kappa*xi_j), with a small stable per-subject part (zeta) and a large momentary per-trial part (xi), applied only when all validities are distinct. (3) POSITIONAL-PRIMACY MINORITY, TIE-ANCHORED and STEEPLY THRESHOLD-GATED: the reading-order fallback fires only on designs that BOTH contain exact advertised-validity ties AND exhibit near-maximal binding ambiguity (A >= 0.80, linear ramp over 0.20, mixture weight capped at 0.35); all-distinct and monotone/anchored designs remain fully collapsed onto the anti-validity core. Response discipline is heterogeneous: softmax(beta) plus lapse epsilon with beta in [0.3, 2.0] and epsilon in [0.08, 0.30], giving pooled decider-follow ~0.69 with the wide between-subject spread that reproduces the follow-protection tail.

def predict(parameters, state, history):
    # Diffuse Mixture Frugality with Strong Interior-Gated Validity Leak
    # (sub-linear coherence variant: sqrt(coherence) leak weighting,
    # steepened tie-anchored primacy gate at A >= 0.80).
    #
    # One-reason decision making: experts consulted one at a time, first
    # strictly discriminating expert decides; no integration across cues.
    # Population-central hierarchy: ANTI-VALIDITY (ascending advertised
    # validity; distrust the weakest expert).
    #
    # Mechanisms:
    #   (1) STRONG INTERIOR-GATED VALIDITY LEAK: when the anti cascade's
    #       first discriminating expert j* carries a strictly interior
    #       validity (min+0.10 < val[j*] < max-0.10), mix toward the TTB
    #       (descending-validity) decider with probability
    #       q = rho_leak * coherence^0.5 * gap_term,
    #       where gap_term = mean adjacent unique-validity gap NORMALIZED
    #       by the validity range (vmax - vmin). The SUB-LINEAR coherence
    #       exponent is the single change vs the accepted base: designs
    #       with coherence ~ 1.0 (the leak anchors: leak-dip, knife-edge,
    #       reversed-cascade designs) keep q unchanged (sqrt(1) = 1),
    #       while moderately coherent designs gain leak mass — e.g.
    #       coherence 0.38 -> effective 0.62 (+62%), coherence 0.6 -> 0.77
    #       (+29%) — pulling their over-predicted decider-follow contrasts
    #       down toward the observed values without touching the anchors.
    #   (2) DIFFUSE HETEROGENEITY: w_j = -val_j + gamma*salience_j
    #       + A^3*(sigma_h*zeta_j + kappa*xi_j), applied only when all
    #       validities are distinct; zeta stable per subject, xi re-drawn
    #       every trial.
    #   (3) POSITIONAL-PRIMACY MINORITY, TIE-ANCHORED + STEEP-THRESHOLD-
    #       GATED (retained from the iter-3/4 experiments, per the
    #       critic's confirmation): the reading-order fallback fires ONLY
    #       on designs that both contain exact validity ties AND have
    #       near-maximal binding ambiguity (A >= 0.80, ramp (A-0.80)/0.20),
    #       with the mixture weight capped at 0.35. All-distinct designs
    #       and monotone/anchored designs keep the pure leak-augmented
    #       anti-validity core.
    #
    # Response discipline: softmax(beta) over the binary winner score plus
    # independent lapse epsilon, with the ACCEPTED BASE's ranges verbatim
    # (beta in [0.3, 2.0], epsilon in [0.08, 0.30]) — the discipline axis
    # was sampled at three points in this loop and the base's setting is
    # the optimum; it is not touched again.
    # No discriminating cue -> exactly 0.5. History is ignored.
    stim = np.asarray(state, dtype=float)
    if stim.ndim != 2 or stim.shape[0] != 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Expects a (2, n_features) stimulus; got shape {stim.shape}."
        )
    n_features = stim.shape[1]

    val = np.asarray(parameters["validities"], dtype=float).ravel()
    if val.shape[0] != n_features:
        raise ValueError(
            f"validities length {val.shape[0]} != n_features {n_features}."
        )

    beta = float(parameters["beta"])
    epsilon = float(parameters["epsilon"])
    gamma = float(parameters["gamma"])
    sigma_h = float(parameters["sigma_h"])
    kappa = float(parameters["kappa"])
    rho_leak = float(parameters["rho_leak"])
    primacy_weight = float(parameters["primacy_weight"])
    tie_break = float(parameters["tie_break"])

    zeta = np.asarray(parameters["zeta"], dtype=float).ravel()
    if zeta.shape[0] != n_features:
        raise ValueError(
            f"zeta length {zeta.shape[0]} != n_features {n_features}."
        )

    n_opts = 2
    a, b = stim[0], stim[1]

    if not np.any(a != b):
        # No discriminating cue: pure guess (lapse mixing leaves a
        # uniform unchanged).
        return np.ones(n_opts) / float(n_opts)

    # ---- helper: average-tie ranks ----
    def avg_ranks(x):
        n = x.shape[0]
        srt = np.argsort(x, kind="stable")
        ranks = np.empty(n, dtype=float)
        i = 0
        while i < n:
            j = i
            while j + 1 < n and x[srt[j + 1]] == x[srt[i]]:
                j += 1
            ranks[srt[i:j + 1]] = 0.5 * (i + j)  # 0-indexed average rank
            i = j + 1
        return ranks

    # ---- positional-salience gradient (early-listed experts favored) ----
    if n_features > 1:
        sal = ((n_features - 1 - np.arange(n_features, dtype=float))
               / (n_features - 1.0)) - 0.5
    else:
        sal = np.zeros(1, dtype=float)

    # ---- binding ambiguity: A = 1 - |Spearman(position, validity)| ----
    if n_features > 1:
        ranks = avg_ranks(val)
        pos_r = np.arange(n_features, dtype=float)
        vp = pos_r - pos_r.mean()
        vr = ranks - ranks.mean()
        denom = np.sqrt(float((vp * vp).sum()) * float((vr * vr).sum()))
        if denom > 1e-12:
            rho = float((vp * vr).sum()) / denom
        else:
            rho = 0.0
        ambiguity = 1.0 - abs(rho)
    else:
        ambiguity = 0.0

    # ---- reversal coherence: |Spearman(validity, validity[::-1])| ----
    if n_features > 1:
        ranks_v = avg_ranks(val)
        ranks_r = avg_ranks(val[::-1])
        dv = ranks_v - ranks_v.mean()
        dr = ranks_r - ranks_r.mean()
        denom2 = np.sqrt(float((dv * dv).sum()) * float((dr * dr).sum()))
        if denom2 > 1e-12:
            rho_rev = float((dv * dr).sum()) / denom2
        else:
            rho_rev = 0.0
        coherence = abs(rho_rev)
    else:
        coherence = 0.0

    # ---- mean adjacent gap over UNIQUE validities, RANGE-NORMALIZED ----
    # gap_term = mean_gap / (vmax - vmin): a scale-free measure of how
    # coarse the validity grid is, so coherent small-range designs are
    # no longer starved of leak mass relative to wide-range designs.
    uvals = np.unique(val)
    distinct = (uvals.size == n_features)
    has_ties = (uvals.size < n_features)
    if uvals.size > 1:
        mean_gap = float(np.mean(np.diff(uvals)))
        v_range = float(uvals[-1] - uvals[0])
        gap_term = mean_gap / v_range if v_range > 1e-12 else 0.0
    else:
        gap_term = 0.0

    pos = np.arange(n_features)
    secondary = pos if tie_break < 0.8 else (n_features - 1 - pos)

    # ---- anti-validity weights with diffuse heterogeneity ----
    # Exact validity ties anchor the distrust order (no distortion);
    # all-distinct lists degrade with the CUBE of binding ambiguity.
    # Small stable part (sigma_h * zeta) + large momentary part
    # (kappa * xi, re-drawn fresh on every trial).
    w = -val + gamma * sal
    if distinct and ambiguity > 0.0:
        amb3 = ambiguity * ambiguity * ambiguity
        xi = np.random.uniform(-1.0, 1.0, size=n_features)
        w = w + amb3 * (sigma_h * zeta + kappa * xi)
    order_anti = np.lexsort((secondary, -w))

    def cascade(order):
        for j in order:
            if a[j] > b[j]:
                return 0
            if b[j] > a[j]:
                return 1
        return None

    winner_anti = cascade(order_anti)

    # ---- this trial's anti-validity carrier (for the leak gate) ----
    j_star = None
    for j in order_anti:
        if a[j] != b[j]:
            j_star = int(j)
            break

    def score_prob(winner):
        scores = np.array([1.0, 0.0]) if winner == 0 else np.array([0.0, 1.0])
        z = beta * (scores - scores.max())
        e = np.exp(z)
        return e / e.sum()

    # Start from the (momentary) anti-validity decider.
    p = score_prob(winner_anti)

    # ---- POSITIONAL-PRIMACY MINORITY (tie-anchored, steep-threshold gate) ----
    # The reading-order fallback is elicited ONLY when the design BOTH
    # contains exact advertised-validity ties AND sits in the near-maximal
    # binding-ambiguity regime (A >= 0.80, linear ramp over 0.20). This is
    # the steepened gate confirmed by the critic: it lowered the
    # anti-misbound-decider follow (Exp 13) in both trial iterations
    # without a real cost on the count-vs-primacy contrast (Exp 15),
    # whose all-distinct validities keep w_eff = 0 exactly.
    if has_ties and ambiguity >= 0.80:
        gate = min(1.0, max(0.0, (ambiguity - 0.80) / 0.20))
    else:
        gate = 0.0
    w_eff = min(primacy_weight * gate, 0.35)
    if w_eff > 0.0:
        winner_prim = cascade(pos)  # earliest-listed expert first
        if winner_prim is not None:
            p = (1.0 - w_eff) * p + w_eff * score_prob(winner_prim)

    # ---- STRONG INTERIOR-GATED VALIDITY LEAK ----
    # Fires only when the anti cascade's carrier is strictly interior:
    # min + 0.10 < val[j*] < max - 0.10. Weakest-carrier and near-top
    # carrier trials keep the leak OFF.
    # SINGLE CHANGE vs the accepted base: the coherence factor enters
    # SUB-LINARLY (coherence**0.5) instead of linearly. High-coherence
    # anchor designs are untouched by construction (sqrt(1) = 1);
    # moderately coherent designs gain leak mass, pulling their
    # over-predicted decider-follow contrasts toward the observed values.
    if j_star is not None and n_features > 1:
        vmin = float(val.min())
        vmax = float(val.max())
        if (vmin + 0.10) < val[j_star] < (vmax - 0.10):
            q = rho_leak * (coherence ** 0.5) * gap_term
            # Numerical validity clamp only (keeps mixture weights proper
            # probabilities on extreme small-n designs); far above the
            # substantive target range on the leak-dip design.
            q = min(max(q, 0.0), 0.75)
            if q > 0.0:
                order_ttb = np.lexsort((secondary, -val))
                winner_ttb = cascade(order_ttb)
                if winner_ttb is not None:
                    p = (1.0 - q) * p + q * score_prob(winner_ttb)

    # ---- heterogeneous response discipline: softmax + lapse ----
    # (base ranges verbatim: beta [0.3, 2.0], epsilon [0.08, 0.30])
    return (1.0 - epsilon) * p + epsilon * (np.ones(n_opts) / float(n_opts))
next_theory.rationale: Minimal-diff edit of the running-best (iter-2) base following the critic's iteration-4 prescription exactly: change ONE thing whose expected effect exceeds the ~0.03 run-to-run noise floor, plus retain the one mechanism the critic explicitly confirmed. (1) THE ONE NEW KNOB — SUB-LINEAR COHERENCE WEIGHTING IN THE LEAK: q = rho_leak * coherence**0.5 * gap_term instead of rho_leak * coherence * gap_term, with rho_leak [0.85, 1.25] and the range-normalized gap_term unchanged. This is a pure normalization-scheme swap inside the arbiter's prescribed leak family. By construction it leaves the high-coherence anchors untouched (coherence ~ 1.0 on the leak-dip design Exp 17, the knife-edge designs Exps 4/1/3, so their near-perfect fits — Exp 17 at -0.198 vs -0.196 observed, Exp 10 at 118.8 vs 116.6 — are preserved), while moderately coherent designs gain leak mass toward the TTB decider: Exp 5 (coherence ~0.38 -> effective 0.62, ~+60% leak on its f4-carrier ladder cells) should pull its +0.06 over-prediction (0.672 vs 0.613 observed) down toward target; Exp 8 (coherence ~0.4-0.5) should deepen its negative misbound-decider contrast from -0.223 toward the observed -0.289; Exp 9/10 (coherence ~0.6 -> effective 0.77, ~+29%) get a small pull-down, with Exp 10's +2.3 overshoot acceptable down to ~110 per the critic's stated floor. (2) RETAINED: the steepened tie-anchored primacy gate from the (rejected) iter-3/4 candidates — threshold lowered from 0.85 to 0.80, ramp widened to /0.20, cap 0.35 — which the critic confirmed moved Exp 13 in the right direction in BOTH trial iterations (0.298 -> 0.268/0.271) without a real cost on Exp 15 (iter 3's 0.1256 with the same gate shows iter 4's 0.071 was Monte Carlo noise, not mechanism).
